newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Agip reports Libyan $2.1 billion gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Agip reports Libyan $2.1 billion gas deal.

text.p: Agip Spa has reached a framework agreement worth $2.1 billion with Libya for the development of Libyan gas fields and the construction of a pipeline, a senior Agip official said.

"Last June, Agip and NOC, the national oil company of Libya, entered into an addendum to their 1974 exploration and production sharing agreement for the joint development of some offshore and onshore natural gas and condensate field," Domenico Tantillo, Vice President, Corporate Planning told a gas seminar in Tunis.

"Production from those fields will be piped to a treatment plant on the Libyan coast. The project envisages the construction of a subsea pipeline from Libya to Italy, where the gas will be introduced into ENI SpA's natural gas network," Tantillo said.
"Agip's capital costs in respect of the project are estimated in the range of $2.1 billion," he added.
"At the moment, 600 million boe (barrels of oil equivalent) of proved undeveloped reserves -- 70 percent natural gas and 30 percent oil and gas condensate -- have been established," he said.
The deal comes in the face of U.S. sanctions signed by U.S. President Bill Clinton which penalises non-U.S. firms from investing $40 million or more a year in the energy industries of Libya and Iran.

"We cannot make any predictions regarding interpretations of the (U.S.) sanctions act, nor of the U.S. government implementation policy. However, ENI does not believe that the sanctions act will have a material adverse effect on the financial condition or results of operations of the company," Tantillo said.
